messages:
erin: quick follow-up from the postmortem — recurring "wave" of pages for the ingestion pipeline during late-night commits. we sketched fixes but need owners + closure criteria.

noah: i'll take alert tuning + short-term mitigation. proposal: change from 1m instant to 8m rolling avg and require 2 consecutive windows. add a 30m post-deploy suppression when `release` tag present. i'll put up a PR with pre/post fire counts by tomorrow.

viv: i'll own dedupe and paging policy. idea: dedupe_key = service:shard_id and collapse identical failures into one incident; also route these to a secondary low-priority rota during the maintenance window (00:00-04:00). will test in staging and target PR by Fri.

ops-lead: please include acceptance criteria in your action items. suggested: 14-day rolling drop >= 70% in pages during the night window, and no increase in user-facing errors. require dashboard snapshots + one runbook drill.

erin: also add correlation bypass: if db-write-error-rate > 0.01 then bypass suppression and escalate immediately. we nearly masked a real outage last time.

noah: config snippet i'll include in the PR:
```yaml
alert: ingest-failure-rate
condition: avg_over_time(8m) > 0.05
require: 2_consecutive_windows
suppression:
  when_tag: release=true
  window: 30m
correlation_bypass:
  - service: db-write-error-rate
    threshold: 0.01
dedupe_key: "service:shard_id"
routing: "ops-low-priority-rota"
```

viv: staging dedupe run collapsed 6 duplicates into one page. routing to the low-priority rota worked in test. i'll post logs and open the PR Friday.

oncall-bot: incident 3032101111 resolved by erin \u2014 duration 1h28m \u2014 postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/3032101111 (auto)

ops-lead: timeline recap — noah PR by tomorrow EOD, viv PR by Fri, runbook drill scheduled next Thurs. checkpoint next_thu 10:30 to review dashboards. /remind @ops-team checkpoint next_thu 10:30

erin: thanks all. owners — update the postmortem action list with PR links, synthetic test results, and screenshots so I can close items against acceptance criteria. :white_check_mark:
